title: BGA 2026 Newsflash
content:
took place in Amsterdam on June 23rd-26th, 2026. BGA, founded in 1970, is an international society dedicated to the scientific study of the interrelationships between genetic mechanisms and behaviour (human and animal), education/training of researchers, and public dissemination of knowledge on genetics and behaviour and their implications for health, development, and education. Overall, BGA 2026 showcased the field’s integration of classical twin/family methods with large-scale genomic, multi-omics, and causal-inference approaches, while highlighting early-career researchers and the societal/public dimensions of behavioural genetics research. 

Dr. Li Tian from the CLIPI group participated in a ” in the BGA 2026 conference. She gave an oral presentation on the recent research findings of direct and indirect parental genetic effects of neuropsychiatric predisposition on child’s externalizing and internalizing behavioural problems using family-based trio datasets in a multi-cohort study.

title: Co‑Creating Field Expertise: Strengthening Herpetological Skills with Emerging Liberian Scientists
content: Herpetological research in West Africa has historically been spatially and temporally patchy, leaving many areas understudied and local ecological knowledge underrepresented in scientific literature. In response, the GCC Lab and the University of Liberia have launched a collaborative initiative focused on strengthening practical field skills among undergraduate biology students. Through hands‑on training and mentorship, participants develop competencies in sampling methods, species identification, and field safety, while also contributing with their local knowledge and perspectives. The program emphasizes mutual learning and aims to support the development of future Liberian scientists equipped to lead conservation efforts in their own country.

title: Upcoming: Workshop on tragedy
content: Suffering, loss, catastrophic consequences; the apparent indifference of reality regarding our sense of the good and the just; human failings, conflicts, and their possible resolution – all of these experiences leave us perplexed and call for understanding, reflection, and human action. Tragic art, and especially staged and written tragedies, have for millennia heeded this call and thus occupied a crucial place in our attempts to explore the dark corners of the human experience – broken worlds and times out of joint.

title: Helsinki SEN Seminar on "Research-related funding applications and instruments" with Prof. Sarah Powell
content: The day began with Professor Sarah Powell's keynote presentation. The keynote included practical tips and personal experiences of building and funding your own research project by applying for grants. She shared a behind-the-scenes look at her impressive list of successfully funded projects, alongside an even longer list of folders containing applications that never received funding. Even for a highly successful researcher such as Prof. Powell, approximately 80-85% of grant applications may not receive funding. She noted that grant writing is a skill that develops through practice, and researchers do not receive funding for projects they never submit. A practical tip is to learn from successful applications, including directly asking colleagues and researchers to share funded proposals. It is also important to identify and stay true to one’s research topic that brings joy, while remaining flexible enough to adapt those interests to different funding opportunities.

title: Artificial Intelligence Collection
content:
• Massively popular: Elements of AI, the course that started it all, is the most popular course in the history of the University of Helsinki. 
  • Made for a wide audience: We have written the materials so that you can get a grasp on artificial intelligence, no matter what your background is. 
  • Created by experts: The courses have been created by experts in the field of AI.   
  • Concrete: The course materials are practical and draw from real life cases. 
  • Non-linear: Courses relate to each other, but do not have to be studied in a certain order. You can complete the whole set of courses or select the ones that are most interesting to you.  
  • Expanding: New courses are added frequently to cover more aspects of artificial intelligence. 
  • Free: Studying the courses does not cost anything. 

    • This micro-credential is perfect for you if 

  • you want learn about AI through practical examples, or 
  • you want get an understanding of artificial intelligence from different perspectives: What AI means for individuals and societies, or 
  • you are wondering how AI might affect your job or your life in the future.

content:
On a guided tour, you’ll journey through millions of years of evolution along the paths of the Evolution Garden, and immerse yourself in a world of scents and colours in the Garden of the senses. You’ll also admire unique lichen and moss gardens, while hearing stories about the garden’s past and present, and the buildings found in the area.

title: “Ilman pölyttäjiä maailma olisi ankea ja väritön” – Uusi näyttely avaa oven pölyttäjien kiehtovaan elämään
content:
Pollinators represent an astonishingly diverse group of animals, many of which possess remarkable abilities despite their small size. Bees can count, bumblebees solve problems, and on distant islands, even lizards can pollinate flowers.

The  exhibition, which combines science and art, offers a wealth of information, stunning visuals, and fun activities for visitors of all ages. Guests can play interactive games like "Identify the Pollinators" and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the museum's impressive collection of specimens. The exhibition is based on a newly illustrated non-fiction book.

– We want to show the world through the eyes of pollinators, says exhibition scriptwriter Mia Rönkä, Adjunct Professor in Environmental Ecology at the University of Turku. Rönkä has written the exhibition’s informational texts and poems.

Although the sensory perceptions, cognitive abilities, and communication methods of pollinators like bees differ from ours as humans, we can still strive to understand and appreciate them as individuals of other species – without anthropomorphizing them, Rönkä explains.

title: Arkadiankadun siltaremontti aiheuttaa muutoksia liikennejärjestelyihin Luonnontieteellisen museon lähistöllä
content:
The renovation will start with the construction of temporary traffic arrangements from Wednesday 7 January onwards. The renovation is expected to be completed in late 2026.

A temporary bridge for pedestrians will be built on the east side of Arkadiankatu over the Baana. The aim is to maintain the pedestrian route on the east side of the bridge until the temporary bridge is operational. Cyclists will also be able to use the bridge.

The Baana route underneath the bridge is expected to remain open for most of the renovation's duration, with some minor exceptions.

There will be changes to the motor vehicle routes by the bridge and around it in January. If possible, should be favoured during the bridge renovation.

Connections to the bus terminals in Kamppi will remain available, but there will be a slight diversion of routes.

Trams 1 and 1T will run via Simonkatu and Kamppi. Lasipalatsi and the Natural History Museum will not be served.

The diversion is due to the renovation of the Arkadiankatu bridge and will remain in place until late 2026. The renovation will not affect HSL's bus services.

title: Ukrainan sota - yliopiston suositukset
content:
The University of Helsinki has condemned the military action by Russia and expressed its support for Ukraine and its university community. We have also expressed our support for Ukraine, together with other Finnish universities, through statements by and the . As a demonstration of support, we have illuminated buildings in the colours of the Ukrainian flag and raised the flag on our premises.

One of the principles of the University of Helsinki is to promote international collaboration in research and higher education, and to support these efforts even in difficult circumstances. Russia’s indefensible military aggression in Ukraine has required exceptional measures, which include those taken in the collaboration between universities.

The University of Helsinki is monitoring both national and EU-level sanctions, adapting our policies and processes accordingly. Together with other Finnish and international universities, the University of Helsinki strives to promote the end of military action in Ukraine, while supporting Ukrainian institutions and people.
